title: Second pass of the key word differs: key read back and forth (and its sliding form), form alternating by pass, odd passes shifted by a constant, tableau alternating by pass, on 666,993 keyword tableaux
k4_result: 28,576,617,156 exact tests with 7+ checks (666,993 alphabets; 5,156 distinct tests on each of 3,334,959 layouts plus 17,064 tableau-alternation tests per alphabet). 0 pass with 7 or more checks (chance predicts about 0.33 at exactly 7 and 0.016 at 8+). Nothing to read. Gauge: 82 pass at 5 checks and 6 at 6 checks (chance predicts about 112 and 5.6). The one-fold test (key written out and then back around the middle of the text, 11 checks) and plain repeating keys of length 38-46 (7-11 checks) are among the tests that fail on every tableau.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s, each on A-Z, KRYPTOS and a different third of the alphabets (222,332-222,333 each, about 9.5 billion tests each): 0, 0, 0 pass with 7+ checks. Gauge at 5 / 6 checks: 44 / 1, 31 / 1, 74 / 1 (chance predicts about 37 / 1.9 each). K4 scaled to a third (27 / 2) sits inside the controls.
planted: 7/7: 16-letter phrase read back and forth (period 32) on a dictionary tableau (13 checks, 67 of 97 letters read, -4.91); 11-letter word alternating Vigenere/Beaufort on KRYPTOS (13 checks, 97 of 97, -4.17); 9-letter word alternating a dictionary tableau and A-Z (15 checks, 97 of 97, -4.15); strip moved by a 10-letter word read back and forth (12 checks, 97 of 97, -4.10); 8-letter word with odd passes shifted by 7, restarting at carved rows (15 checks, 97 of 97, -4.39); 13-letter word back and forth with row restart (16 checks, 70 of 97, -4.58); 49 random key letters written out and back (11 checks, found by the exact test; only 2 new letters, so no reading). Each among 16,676 alphabets. The true setting always had the most checks and no wrong reading scored as well. It was NOT always the single survivor: 1-19 weaker settings that the same key also satisfies passed too (for example the A-Z passes of the tableau-alternating message show up as a period-18 key on plain A-Z).
scope_limits: The tableau alphabet must be A-Z, KRYPTOS or one of 666,991 dictionary keyword alphabets (plain or the two transposition-mixed forms), in layouts M/M, M/AZ, AZ/M, M/KR, KR/M; hidden alphabets are not covered. Mirror key and its sliding form: period 16-52 with every start letter and all three ways of turning (word length about 9-26), one fold over the whole text, or restart at the carved rows (K4 letters 1, 5, 36, 67); only (period, start) pairs with 7+ checks are decided (1,790 distinct mirror tests and 1,424 sliding tests per view); pairs with fewer checks, mostly at the longer periods, are not decided. Sliding form: whole-text count only. Form alternation: Vigenere/Beaufort, Vigenere/variant, Beaufort/variant, Beaufort/minus-Beaufort, word length 2-52, every start, whole text or carved-row restart, where 7+ checks exist. Shift: one constant on odd passes only. Tableau alternation: keyword tableau against A-Z or KRYPTOS only (not two dictionary tableaux), pure tableaux (plain, cipher and key on the same alphabet), key letter by own alphabet or A-Z label. A change on any schedule other than every pass (every row, every word, every third pass), three or more kinds of pass, a second pass that is a different word, and any transposition are not covered.

negative.family: key word with a different second pass (mirror / alternating form / alternating tableau)
negative.hypothesis: K4 uses one key word whose second pass differs from the first: read backwards, in the other cipher form, moved by a constant, or on the other tableau, so the key only repeats after two passes
negative.scope: 666,993 keyword alphabets (A-Z, KRYPTOS, dictionary, transposition-mixed) x 5 layouts; key read back and forth with period 16-52, every start and turn, one fold over the text, carved-row restart, and its sliding form; plain period 18-52; form alternating by pass (4 pairings, word 2-52); odd passes shifted by a constant; tableau alternating with A-Z or KRYPTOS (9 form pairings, 2 key-letter conventions); 28.6 billion exact tests with 7+ checks on the 24 clue letters
negative.outcome: Dead in scope: 0 tests pass with 7+ checks (chance predicts 0.35); gauge at 5-6 checks 88 against about 118 predicted. Controls: 3 shuffled K4s on a third of the alphabets each give 0 at 7+ and 45, 32, 75 in the gauge; planted 7/7 found with the true setting on top and the message read back

follow_ups: The same equal-key-letter engine can test a change on a schedule other than every pass at almost no cost: form or tableau switching at each carved row, at each plaintext word break of the clues (EAST / NORTHEAST / BERLIN / CLOCK), or every third pass (three kinds of pass in rotation).

Second pass is a DIFFERENT word on the same tableau but the two words are tied by a rule (second word = first word enciphered by itself, or its Atbash, or its keyword-alphabet image): each rule is again a set of equal-key-letter ties after a known letter map, testable exactly with word lengths up to about 17.
